analysis:
The change to docs/provider/cli-reference.md is documentation only. Head adds a paragraph after the `darkbloom update` section (head lines 1804-1810) and edits the `[provider] auto_update` row (head line 2148). The paragraph says `darkbloom update` on a Mac running the cluster service now asks the service supervisor to restart into the installed release with the other Mac, after the pair has drained. It prints progress for at most `--timeout` seconds, and a deferral exits 1. The auto_update row now mentions a coordinated pair update at the update slot.

The supplied units are the base text only, plus the patch excerpt. No code was supplied, so none of the following is verified here:
- The implementation in UpdateCommand.swift and ClusterServiceUpdateRequest. The doc claims a supervisor restart request and a pair drain, but it describes no auth or integrity mechanism for that request.
- The unchanged pre-existing statement that the update path verifies bundle, binary and mlx.metallib hashes before replacement, which is the T-013/T-034/T-043 area.
- The cluster peer-to-peer restart or drain coordination. A malicious peer or local process could trigger restarts or availability loss (A-018, TB-012-adjacent).

No threat-model assertion is contradicted by the doc text. Update integrity (SelfUpdater hash verification) is stated as unchanged. The new coordinated restart adds a possible availability and control-channel surface, but it is only documented here, not shown. The next pass should check any code PR for the supervisor request channel's authentication, the peer-restart authorization, and the bounded timeout.

No finding is reported, because a documentation-only change with no visible control regression does not qualify. I am flagging deeper review only for the unsupplied implementation.
